description: With the block duration from the modem, a received EOT counts from the start of the D_PDU's block (the block's arrival less one block), plus the D_PDU's share of the block, not from the arrival of its header.
note: Conn 1 binds SAP 5 for non-ARQ and gets S_BIND_ACCEPTED (A-0041, A-0047). Every received D_PDU is a single-segment NON-ARQ-DATA (type 7, address size 4, C_PDU ID as stated, reception window 20) from 0.0.1.3 to 0.0.1.9 whose segment is a DATA C_PDU holding a DATA S_PDU from SAP 9 to SAP 9 with U_PDU "hi" (31 bytes, as in dts-rx-vdcd-end-after-burst-end). burst_started gives block_ms (corpus 0.31.0), so each EOT counts from the latest instant its D_PDU can have started on air: the arrival time of the bytes_received holding its first byte, less block_ms, plus ceil(offset x block_ms / bytes in that bytes_received) (interp C-1289); the burst's estimate is the earliest end time (C-0843). After the burst, conn 1's S_UNIDATA_REQUEST (priority 0 to SAP 5 at 0.0.1.3, U_PDU "hello", no confirmation) is queued: no SIS output (A-0095, K-0096), dts.ttd starts at its TTD (C-1050), and with the channel busy until the estimate csma.vdcd_end runs to it (K-0073, K-0111). At its expiry VDCD clears last and the D_PDUs heard were addressed to another node, so rule 3 gives lbt_wait_vdcd_ms 3000 (K-0071, K-0073). burst_started at 1000 gives block_ms 4800. The block at 6000 holds 62 bytes: D_PDU A (C_PDU ID 1, EOT 20) at offset 0, anchor 6000 - 4800 + 0 = 1200, end 11200; D_PDU B (C_PDU ID 2, EOT 20) at offset 31, anchor 1200 + ceil(31 x 4800 / 62) = 3600, end 13600. The block at 10800 holds D_PDU C (C_PDU ID 3, EOT 10) at offset 0 of 31 bytes: anchor 6000, end 11000. The estimate is 11000 (C-0843), against 15800 under C-1024 alone. The burst ends at 10800 (eom, 2 blocks) with nothing queued, so no output. The request at 10900 starts dts.ttd and csma.vdcd_end 100 ms; at 11000 rule 3 gives csma.lbt_wait 3000.
